_comment: Short 2 in docs/CONTENT.md — the January reset. The first line is carried in `variants` because tts.mjs treats that as the hook; here the hook IS the first thing drawn.
_injury: Slipped on ice, which is also why it is January. House style: the injury has to earn its place in the story, not just be different from the last one.
_numbers: A $1,000 deductible and the SAME $400 visit in both months — that is the whole point. What changes is the split: $100 you / $300 insurance in November, $400 you / $0 insurance in January. An earlier cut showed $40 against $400 as though the PRICE had changed, which is the exact confusion this Short exists to undo.
_jargon: e10 names the word and e11 defines it. An earlier cut named it and stopped, which taught a label rather than a meaning. The definition is the last thing said before the offer, because by then the viewer has watched the mechanism twice and the sentence lands on something they already understand.
_hold: e6 asks a question and refuses to answer it. It is a retention beat — the payoff is two lines away and the viewer has a reason to stay for it — and it is also honest, because the answer genuinely is the definition of the word the Short is about.

variants.ice: Your body does not know it is January. Your insurance does.

body.text: Every year, you pay the first chunk yourself. Here, a thousand dollars.
By November you had filled it.
So when you went in, the hospital billed four hundred.
You paid one hundred. Your insurance paid the other three hundred.
Why did they pay three hundred of it? It will make sense in a second.
Because on the first of January, they tip the bucket out.
Same knee, same clinic, same four hundred dollar bill.
This time you pay all four hundred, and your insurance pays nothing.
That bucket has a name. It is your deductible.
What you pay yourself each year before your insurance starts paying its share. Full bucket, they pay. Empty bucket, you pay.
